Since Jony Ive left Apple in 2019, the company has lacked a true head of design. For a while, former Chief Operating Officer Jeff Williams handled design duties until he left the company last year. Since then, as Bloomberg's Mark Gurman notes, CEO John Ternus has shown a strong interest in Apple's two design teams—Industrial Design and Human Interface.

This story actually begins before John Ternus became CEO, which was just over a month ago. It started when Jeff Williams resigned as COO. The company announced at the time that the teams would report to then-CEO Tim Cook, but in practice Ternus was reportedly running point. It was one of his key responsibilities during his transition to CEO.

Of course, Ternus's interest in design is not surprising, given his background overseeing hardware engineering. But Gurman describes Ternus's level of involvement as 'deeply engaged,' and he frequently visits in person to work with the teams:

This stands in stark contrast to former CEO Tim Cook—who, per Bloomberg, visited the design studio roughly once a month.

Ternus 'deeply engaged' with Apple's design teams

Ternus is also focused on replenishing the design teams with fresh blood, as the company has lost significant talent to other firms. The most prominent example is Alan Dye, who left to join Meta, while OpenAI has also poached a number of employees from Apple. To reinvigorate the teams, Apple has promoted several junior designers and hired new talent from outside.

Throughout all this, the company has still not actively searched for someone to replace Jony Ive in a role akin to Chief Design Officer. According to Bloomberg, there are no active recruiting efforts underway. Rather, the company has appointed Molly Anderson and Steve Lemay to lead Industrial Design and Human Interface, respectively, with Ternus personally serving as the ultimate decision-maker on design matters.

Although Ternus does not come from a traditional design background, his investment in design signals one thing: design will continue to be a cornerstone of Apple's executive agenda.
